tei:titleStmt.tei:title: 4: Behold you are beautiful, my beloved, behold you are beautif

tei:availability.tei:p: Published by Sefaria under CC-BY, which Sefaria defines as Creative Commons Attribution 3.0.

tei:div.tei:p: Behold you are beautiful, my beloved, behold you are beautiful, your eyes are like doves from within your kerchief; your hair is like a flock of goats descending from Mount Gilead. Your teeth are like a counted flock which have come up from the washing; all of which are perfect and none are blemished among them. Like a scarlet thread are your lips, and your speech is comely; like a slice of pomegranate are your cheeks from within your kerchief. Your neck is like the Tower of David, built as a model of beauty; a thousand shields are hung upon it, all the quivers of the mighty. Your bosom is like two fawns, twins of a gazelle who pasture among the roses. Until the sun spreads and the shadows flee; I will go to Mount Moriah and to the hill of frankincense. You are completely beautiful, my beloved, and are without blemish. With me [will you come] from Lebanon O bride, with me from Lebanon will you come; you will look from the peak of Amana, from the peaks of Senir of Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of leopards. You captured my heart, my sister, O bride; you captured my heart with but one of your eyes, with one necklace of your necklaces. How beautiful is your love my sister, O bride; how superior is your love to wine, and the fragrance of your oils to all perfumes. Your lips drip flowing honey, O bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the fragrance of your garments is like the fragrance of Lebanon. A locked garden is my sister, O bride; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain. Your arid fields are a pomegranate orchard with luscious fruits; henna with spikenard. Spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all the trees of frankincense; myrrh and aloes with all the major spices. You are a garden spring, a well of living waters; and flowing streams from Lebanon. Awake, wind from the north and come, wind from the south, blow upon my garden so that its fragrance may flow; let my beloved come to his garden, and eat its luscious fruit.

tei:note.tei:p: God speaks to Israel and praises her, declaring that He is pleased with her offerings.—Rashi

Your characteristics are like the dove which is loyal to its mate. When it is slaughtered it does not fidget but stretches forth her neck submissively. So have you bent your shoulder to bear My yoke and My awe.—Rashi

Even the most common people [whose merit is concealed] among you, are as dearly beloved to Me as Yaakov and his sons who descended the slopes of Mount Gilead when they were pursued by Laban. [Genesis 31:23]—Rashi

This is said in reference to the 12,000 men who fought against Midian [Numbers 31:5]; not one of them was ‘blemished’ even with suspicion of lewdness. So chaste were they that they brought offerings of atonement even for evil thoughts they might have had.— Rashi
As numerous as a pomegranate’s seeds are the merits of even the most unworthy among you.—Rashi

The ‘Tower of David’ refers to the righteous who stand erect as a tower even amid hardship and persecution, without yielding to idolatrous practices. Thus the Sages of Israel serve as a model of behavior for all to behold.—Rashi

According to Rashi שְׁנֵי שָׁדַיךְ , your two breasts, refers to Moshe and Aharon who nursed the nation of Israel in their infant state as a people. They are likened to the twins of a gazelle because they were equal to each other. Others say that it refers to the Written and Oral Torah, which like twins complement one another.
When Israel stood at Sinai to accept the Torah, they were all in a state of total perfection. There were no lame, nor blind nor deaf, nor imbeciles, nor lepers, nor those who were unclean.—Midrash
God says to His people, “With Me will you be exiled from the Temple [Lebanon].” (See Targum Onkelos to Deuteronomy 3:25 where he translates וְהַלְבָנוֹן as בֵּית מַקְדָשָׁא .)
The Almighty says to Israel, “You captured My heart with but one of your [many] virtues, with your fulfillment of even one of the precepts that adorn you like a necklace.—Rashi
The sweetness of Torah flows from your lips.

Garments refer to מִדוֹת , character traits, which like garments are not inborn but must be acquired and worn. The fragrance of garments symbolize the impression they make on others. Similarly, one’s מִדוֹת should be fragrant, leaving a pleasing impression on others.— Vilna Gaon
This is said in reference to the modesty of the women in Israel who shun immorality.
Even the least gifted [the dry ones] among you are like a pomegranate orchard with luscious fruits.
Israel appeals to the Holy One, blessed is He, to once again dwell in the Temple [His garden] and savor the offerings [the luscious fruits] which we will bring there.
